title: How should differences from the upstream ownership baseline be classified?
question: How should differences from the upstream ownership baseline be classified?
answer:
FND-Q24B: A legacy room row that differs from upstream and carries no authored intent is a conflict until intent is declared. The owner chose S-00G's Option A: "conflict - Every undeclared difference is a conflict until intent is declared. Safest, but the first upgrade of every legacy room stops on each such row." The companion placement question (whether a divergence disposition and any authorizing ADR citation live in the map or in the decision/report that owns the disposition) was not covered by this answer; S-00G's recommendation to keep it outside the map stays a recommendation. The field shape that carries the verdict without a status-shaped field is settled within S-00G at implementation under the Q23 guards. On 2026-09-22 he had ruled the question stays live under S-00G as an ownership-origin question.
PW-2: FND-Q24B stays live under S-00G, relabeled an ownership-origin-model question. It is neither parked behind nor folded into Portable Workbench; the two are independent. The existing FND-Q24B handoff stays valid for a separate deep-dive chat. No priority order between them was set.
FND-Q24: Two ownership origins (upstream Workbench, project-local) and three classifications (portable invariants and defaults, project bindings, optional extensions). A deliberate change to a baseline assignment is divergence and needs an explicit disposition. Define relationships, including primary ownership and supporting roles, rather than the full cross-product. "An added row is a mechanical comparison fact"; "a core artifact type does not by itself prove compatibility." Renamed the Ownership origin model on 2026-09-22.
